newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Record of Russia-Ukraine Black Sea Fleet deals.
newsitem.headline: Record of Russia-Ukraine Black Sea Fleet deals.

text.p: An agreement between Russia and Ukraine giving Moscow the right to lease the Ukrainian port of Sevastopol for 20 years for its ships is aimed at ending years of bargaining about the former Soviet Black Sea Fleet.
Following is a brief record of major events in the protracted dispute over the fleet:

-- May 1992 -- The row starts when the then-Ukrainian leader, Leonid Kravchuk, orders the creation of a national navy based on the Black Sea Fleet and Russian President Boris Yeltsin orders the-then joint military command of the post-Soviet Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) to take the fleet under its control.
-- August 1992 -- Kravchuk and Yeltsin sign a deal near the Black Sea resort of Yalta under which the fleet is withdrawn from CIS command and taken under command of the two states.
-- June 1993 -- The two leaders decide at a meeting in Moscow to split the fleet 50:50.
-- June 1995 -- Russia and Ukraine strike another deal under which Moscow takes 81.7 percent of the fleet while Kiev takes 18.3 percent. Russia announces plans to buy out the Ukrainian share.

-- June 1996 -- Ukraine introduces a new constitution barring foreign military bases from the country's territory. But parliament in a clear compromise with Moscow later adopts an amendment allowing temporary foreign bases under special agreements.
